accuracy.evidence: Research is described as found: Tajfel et al. (1971) grouped 14-15-year-old boys on trivial criteria (dot estimates, Klee vs Kandinsky) and most allocated more points to their own group, often choosing maximum difference over maximum joint profit; Billig and Tajfel (1973) used explicitly random (coin-toss style) allocation and still found in-group favouritism, which is the lab's framing. Allport and Postman (1947) described levelling and sharpening in serial retelling. Passive/assertive/aggressive definitions match standard PSHE usage. Numeric answers t-b, k+k*k, s*k and 2*b-t stay positive at every range corner (t 10-14, b 8-10).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets hostile attribution bias, reading one unclear cue as rejection (step 1 prediction 'They definitely do not want me here', challenge 'worst' and 'tit', p1); the belief that groups only form for good reasons (step 2 prediction, challenge 'better' and 'knew', m2); that passing gossip on unchanged or 'asking around' is harmless (challenge 'exact' and 'ask', m4); and that assertive means loud or that quiet is weak (challenge 'weak', 'none', 'shout').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcues combines five different mechanics: tapping people at a table to reveal graded cues, a points slider between a coin-toss in-group and out-group, a rumour chain with Pass it on / Stop it here and a harm bar, a three-part reply that moves a passive-assertive-aggressive gauge, and a three-step choice path. flagupst (351, bystanders), flagmask (364, one person's hidden feelings), flagroles (396) and flagbelong (482) use none of these; the 30% shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each action gives immediate, specific feedback: each cue card is graded (WELCOME, STRONG: CHECK IT, PROVES NOTHING) with what it could mean; the split reports where the child sits against Tajfel's finding; passing the rumour to the end fills the harm bar and asks them to stop it sooner; each reply part names itself passive, assertive or aggressive as the needle moves; wrong path choices explain the cost and keep the child at that point.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions, each tested by the scene that follows: the best first thought when the talk stops (tempting: they do not want me), whether coin-toss teams still favour their own (tempting: a coin toss means nothing), what happens to a story over five retellings (tempting: stays the same), and the best first move when left out (tempting: post about it). Done messages say whether the prediction held.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating Challenge questions with rotated answer order and 12 m= messages, one for each wrong answer (aggr, pass, worst, tit, exact, ask, better, knew, fit, shout, weak, none), e.g. 'Asking around spreads the rumour further, even if you mean well.' Feedback is in a polite live region with a streak counter.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and defines each term in context (social cue, gossip, passive, aggressive, assertive) with concrete lunch-table and party examples, passing the learner kid FK limit. Adult text names hostile attribution bias, cites the guidance and the studies, and gives the vocabulary list.

no_filler.evidence: The four kid paragraphs map one-to-one to the topic's strands: reading cues and checking them, in-group/out-group pull, gossip as bonding with costs, and assertive versus aggressive responses to exclusion. The numeric items model real things in the lab (points split and gap, how fast a rumour spreads) rather than decoration.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark (r1403/cue-phone-*, cuecv*.png) show four people above the table with revealed cues as full-width cards, a draggable slider with buttons as an alternative, the gauge with all three labels clear of the arc, and three full-width reply slots. All moves are buttons below the canvas; the walk gate passed on phone and desktop.

accessibility.evidence: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13. Every move has a labelled button (for example 'Change the opening. Now: "It's fine, I guess…"' and 'Stop the rumour here and say: I do not know that is true'); the canvas aria-label and live region read each cue, split, rumour hop and gauge result; colour is never the only signal because every zone and cue is labelled in text.
